title: Metis Agent, open source, that boosts AI/LLM coding performance by 50%
content:
English · 简体中文
A coding agent that searches, remembers, executes, and verifies across terminal and desktop.
Quick start · Benchmark & Comparison · Key features · Documentation
Standalone application with built-in Metis CLI and Server runtime (no Node.js required):
- macOS (Apple Silicon): Download Metis-*-macos-arm64.dmg from the latest GitHub Release and drag to Applications.
- Windows (x64): Download Metis-*-win-x64-setup.exe or.zip from the latest GitHub Release.
CLI installation
Requires Node.js >=22.19.0.
npm install -g @wholiver_hu/metis
metis
Run in any repository or directory:
metis "Explain this repository"
metis @src/main.ts "Review this file"
git diff | metis -p "Review this diff"
Use /login for subscription providers or configure an API key. See Quickstart for the complete guide.
In a controlled benchmark run using the same model (DeepSeek V4 Flash), same 89 real-world tasks, identical budget, and environment:
- Plan & Build Dual Workflows — Safely investigate in read-only Plan mode, then execute approved plans with a live-updating checklist in Build mode.
- Dual Interface for Terminal & Desktop — Work directly in your terminal via the rich interactive TUI, or use the dedicated React/Vite Desktop workspace on macOS and Windows.
- Recursive Multi-Agent System — Native named agents (coordinator ,planner ,implementer ,reviewer ,verifier ) with L0→L4 recursive delegation and Git Worktree isolation.
- Durable Memory & Resumable Sessions — Project knowledge and decisions persist in SQLite across restarts, context compactions, and session forks.
- Extensible & Model-Agnostic — Use any LLM provider (OpenAI, Anthropic, DeepSeek, OrcaRouter, Gemini, Groq, Ollama, vLLM) and extend with TypeScript plugins, Agent Skills, and MCP.
- Benchmark-Grade Reliability — Automated verification gates, video evidence inspection, and full Terminal-Bench & Harbor evaluation readiness.
See the documentation index for every guide.
Developer information
npm run build                 # Compile TypeScript and copy runtime assets
npm test                      # Run the Vitest suite
npm run clean                 # Remove compiled output
npm run build:binary          # Build the standalone binary
npm --prefix desktop run dev  # Start the React/Vite Desktop app in development
npm --prefix desktop run build # Build the renderer and Electron artifact
The package exports the Node.js SDK from @wholiver_hu/metis and the RPC entry point from @wholiver_hu/metis/rpc-entry.
Contributions are welcome. See CONTRIBUTING.md for development, Extension and Package integration, testing, and AI-assisted contribution guidance.

report.summary: Metis is an open-source AI coding agent that boosts LLM coding performance by 50% using recursive multi-agent workflows, durable memory, and terminal/desktop interfaces.
report.background: AI coding agents have proliferated, but many struggle with context loss, poor execution verification, and single-interface limitations. Metis addresses these by combining plan/build dual workflows, a recursive multi-agent architecture (coordinator, planner, implementer, reviewer, verifier), and SQLite-based durable memory that survives restarts and context compaction. It is model-agnostic, supporting OpenAI, Anthropic, DeepSeek, Gemini, Groq, Ollama, vLLM, and more, while offering both a rich terminal TUI and a React/Vite desktop app. The project claims a 50% performance improvement over baseline in a controlled benchmark using DeepSeek V4 Flash across 89 real-world tasks with identical budget and environment. Its MIT license and plugin/MCP extensibility position it as a flexible alternative to proprietary agent tools.
key_points: Metis introduces Plan and Build dual workflows: Plan mode safely investigates code read-only, while Build mode executes approved plans with a live-updating checklist, reducing risky autonomous actions.

It uses a recursive multi-agent system with named native agents (coordinator, planner, implementer, reviewer, verifier) and L0-L4 recursive delegation, plus Git Worktree isolation for safe parallel changes.

Durable memory and resumable sessions persist project knowledge and decisions in SQLite across restarts, context compactions, and session forks, addressing the common problem of lost context in long coding sessions.
The tool is model-agnostic and extensible: it works with any LLM provider and supports TypeScript plugins, Agent Skills, and MCP, making it adaptable to existing workflows.

Installation is flexible: a standalone binary for macOS/Windows, an npm CLI (Node.js >=22.19.0), and a Node.js SDK/RPC entry for integration. It is MIT-licensed and benchmark-oriented with automated verification gates.
report.impact: For AI developers, Metis offers a transparent, verifiable alternative to closed coding agents, with a 50% claimed performance boost on identical budgets—meaning better output without higher compute costs. Its recursive delegation and durable memory could reduce iterative debugging and context re-injection, improving developer productivity on complex codebases. For regular users, the desktop app and TUI lower the entry barrier to AI-assisted code review and repository understanding. As open-source, it may spark community-driven improvements, and its MCP support means it can plug into the broader agent ecosystem. However, 50% benchmarks should be scrutinized per task type, and teams should validate on their own repositories before adopting.
report.tools: Watch the Metis GitHub repository (github.com/Wholiver/metis) for releases and benchmarks. For hands-on testing, install via npm (`npm install -g @wholiver_hu/metis`) or download the desktop binary. Companion tools to explore include Terminal-Bench and Harbor for benchmark-grade evaluation, plus MCP servers and TypeScript plugin APIs for extending behavior. If you use Ollama or vLLM, Metis can be tested entirely locally.
